A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MIND and include its method, experiments, and Appendices A–D. The readable text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original continued-pretraining and from-scratch training experiments, benchmark evaluations, and dialogue-quality analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds generator-size, dialogue-length, and stronger-pretrained-model analyses.

M1.justification: The seven conversational prompts, 500-token input chunks, heuristic filtering, and pretraining framework remain unchanged. Alternative generator sizes and the Nemotron-generated release do not introduce a new algorithm or training objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use OpenWebMath, MathPile, and the same mathematical, specialized-knowledge, general-reasoning, and coding benchmarks. The added model configurations retain this coverage. The announced 138B-token release is not reported as a new training or evaluation corpus in the experiments.

E2.justification: v2 Table 15 adds raw OWM-14B continued training as an explicit control in the expanded DeepSeekMath comparison. Rephrase is not a newly evaluated baseline: its results already appeared in v1 Tables 5, 9, and 10, before being incorporated into v2 Table 1.

E3.justification: v2 adds an 8B dialogue-generator configuration and reports additional 500B-token continuation experiments starting from DEEPSEEKMATH-7B. These extend existing experimental recipes; the main training budgets, data mixtures, and metrics remain unchanged. The shot counts made explicit in Section 3.2 were already documented in v1 Appendix A.2.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands checks of alternative explanations: Section 5 tests dependence on a 70B versus 8B generator, Appendix C.2 examines dialogue length versus accuracy, and Appendix C.4 adds a stronger-base-model comparison. It also expands the existing human/LLM quality audit and replaces the Two Professors example in Appendix D.

E5.justification: Neither version reports new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The 20-context audit and overall Spearman correlation of 0.03 remain. v2's additional correlation of 0.82 is a new result using an existing statistical measure, not a changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantive findings on model dependence and dialogue quality: Table 6 reports 22.37 GSM8K and 5.72 MATH for the 8B-generator variant; Table 13 adds dialogue-length measurements; Appendix C.3 adds 96%/98% correctness figures and correlation 0.82; Table 15 adds a stronger-model raw-data control. These are additional reported results under their stated conditions, not improvements to retained scores, which remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2 retains equivalent generation, filtering, and pretraining definitions. Neither version contains a changed theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical derivation for MIND.

C1.justification: The abstract adds a contribution announcing release of 138B synthetic tokens. The original 64B-token experimental corpus description, headline performance gains, knowledge-gap claim, and main conclusions remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 argues that gains do not require the large generator, acknowledges knowledge distillation in synthetic generation, and explains why dialogue length alone cannot account for performance. It also adds stronger-model applicability and high-correctness interpretations. Existing knowledge-gap explanations and coding limitations remain.

D1.justification: v1 supplies prompts and implementation details but no dataset-release route. v2 adds a dataset-access link, accompanying documentation link, and provenance for a 138B-token corpus generated with Nemotron4-340B-Instruct. This substantially expands resource-access information, although the release is distinct from the Llama3-generated corpus used in the reported experiments.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly compares MIND with Dai et al.'s dialog inpainting, distinguishing complementary reasoning and conversational diversity. It also adds citations including Nemotron, Self-Refine, Llemma, Gemma, and data-curation work. The overall positioning as scalable synthetic pretraining remains.

P1.justification: The Rephrase discussion moves from the ablations into Section 4, several paragraphs are condensed, and new analyses receive local subsections. Contact information and conference headers change. The overall section organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 merges the former standalone Rephrase comparison into Table 1 and adds tables for generator size, dialogue length, and stronger-model continuation. Other displays mainly move or receive new numbers. Figure 3 retains its plotted values but loses the second line of several category labels, reducing readability.

improvement.justification: The smaller-generator and dialogue-length analyses address specific gaps in v1, while the closer prior-work comparison and data-access information improve usefulness. However, the released corpus uses a different generator from the experiments. The stronger-model evidence also has unresolved reporting problems: Table 15 repeats Table 14's synthetic scores despite different stated starting models, and its claimed 3.43-point general-reasoning gain conflicts with the table's 3.69-point difference.
